actionable.title: Prevent sensitive filenames from entering evidence metadata
actionable.problem: The promise that evidence omits sensitive workspace filenames is not upheld by all output fields. For an untracked .env.SYNTHETIC_PRIVATE_SITE file, is_forbidden_tracked identifies the .env variant, but forbidden_workspace_files.suffixes serializes .synthetic_private_site. A staged forbidden file is copied verbatim into forbidden_tracked_files.items. A prohibited file under scripts/bootstrap/* also appears by its full path in policy_sha256; the newly added candidate mode serializes that inventory without a prohibited-name gate. Thus a failed verification or an unapproved candidate can publish the very filename the dedicated workspace check is supposed to minimize. This is a static data-flow finding using synthetic example names, not an observation of actual sensitive data. The suffix/tracked-name/ordinary inventory behavior predates the base; candidate serialization is added by this PR.
actionable.fix: Use fixed classification labels for environment-file variants instead of arbitrary suffixes, and publish counts or fixed categories rather than forbidden tracked paths. Reject candidate generation when its inventory contains prohibited inputs, and ensure failed receipt/baseline diagnostic fields do not reintroduce those filenames through policy hashes or path-difference lists. Add harmless regressions for an untracked .env.<private-marker>, a staged prohibited filename, and a prohibited file matched by scripts/bootstrap/*; assert marker absence from every written artifact.

actionable.title: Propagate Bash uv sync failures before issuing final success
actionable.problem: With a matching preflight and AUTO_INSTALL=1, the Bash synchronization command is the left operand of an && list: (cd tools/research && uv sync --frozen >/dev/null) && ok. Bash errexit does not terminate for that failed conditional operand. A nonzero uv sync therefore continues through the remaining wrapper steps and final verifier. If a previous tools/research/.venv directory already exists and the other checks pass, the verifier only tests that directory presence and can return 0, so the wrapper reports overall success despite the failed requested synchronization. The Windows entry point explicitly preserves this failure; the Bash synthetic dispatcher never generates a failing sync, leaving the counterpart uncovered. This control-flow issue is inherited unchanged from the base, but remains relevant to the reviewed bootstrap failure boundary.
actionable.fix: Capture and immediately propagate the uv sync failure in the Bash wrapper, preserving the failing status and preventing a final success receipt for that wrapper run. Extend the existing harmless Bash dispatcher to model a nonzero sync exit and assert a nonzero wrapper result and no final verifier call, as the PowerShell tests already do.
